title: Optimize eval sentinel ecosystem and trigger orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a production-ready "sentinel ecosystem" for Optimize evaluations: a structured set of cohort, prompt-level, and infrastructure signals that can gate A/B rollouts and trigger automated remediation (traffic reduction, gradual rollback, or immediate fail-open). The goal is to provide a deterministic, auditable decision path so product teams can ship model/quantization/config changes with clear, actionable stop/mitigation rules.

Scope of work:
- Define sentinel types (quality, safety, latency, cost) and canonical metrics for each.
- Specify stratified prompt/cohort sampling rules to ensure coverage of high-risk cohorts (enterprise flows, low-frequency tokens, non-English locales).
- Define statistical tests, required power, and multiple-testing corrections for A/B/Canary comparisons.
- Specify numeric regression thresholds and graded action (warning, throttle, rollback).
- Define orchestration behavior: ordered actions, cooldown windows, alerting, and audit log schemas.
- Produce an acceptance checklist for SRE/DS/Eng/PM signoff and a rollout cookbook for Solutions/CS.

Why now and product impact:
Optimize v2 increases autonomy for model tuning and quantization. Without strong eval contract and automated stop rules we risk user-visible regressions and support load. This work reduces incident risk, shortens mean time to detect regressions, and standardizes runbooks for safe rollouts across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments.

Primary stakeholders and reviewers:
- PM: Aisha Patel (owner)
- Eng: Luca Martinez (assignee), Mei Chen (runtime), Diego Alvarez (console)
- DS/Evals: Nora Kim (stat tests), Rahul Desai (prompt cohorts)
- SRE & Security: Priya Singh (SLOs), Omar Khaled (audit/KMS)

Non-goals:
- Building UI for custom sentinel creation (console work will be separate ticket).
- Replacing diagnostics/trace pipelines; we assume existing trace + metrics ingestion is available.

Implementation notes / trade-offs considered:
- Conservative thresholds reduce false negatives but increase manual rollbacks; we bias toward safety for enterprise customers.
- Multiple-test corrections: we prefer sequential gate design (tiered canaries) over harsh FDR corrections to preserve signal for small cohorts.
- For latency/cost signals we use relative change windows (percent increase) with absolute floors to avoid noisy small-sample triggers.

Key definitions (canonical):
- Prompt sentinel: aggregated signal computed over a labeled prompt set (owner-specified), evaluated daily and during canaries.
- Cohort sentinel: grouped by customer/locale/intent tokenization with minimum sample size (n>=500).
- Safety sentinel: binary/error-classification signals (toxic outputs, PII leakage) using validated detectors; treated as high-priority immediate-fail triggers.
- Performance sentinel: response-time percentiles (p50/p95/p99), and token-generation failure rate.

Deliverables:
- This PRD (finalized) + an acceptance checklist.
- A sentinel mapping table (CSV) listing metric, owner, detection query, threshold, action.
- Orchestration cookbook outlining stepwise remediation actions and example timelines.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel catalog: CSV delivered with at least one example for each sentinel type (quality, safety, latency, cost) and owner assigned
Sampling spec: stratified prompt/cohort sampling doc that covers enterprise, long-tail, and non-English cohorts with min sample sizes and heuristics
Stat test spec: defined primary statistical test(s) for A/B with required power >= 80% for main signal, alpha per-gate <= 0.01, and multiple-testing plan for sequential canaries

Thresholds: numeric regression thresholds defined for primary metrics: quality delta (absolute)  >= 2% WER/acceptance OR relative metric delta >= 5% depending on metric, safety binary triggers cause immediate mitigation
Orchestration rules: documented ordered actions (alert -> throttle to 10% -> stop and rollback) with cooldowns and minimum monitoring windows (e.g., 30m warmup + 6h observe)
Automated playbook: console hooks (webhook + dashboard links) for each action and audit entries captured in the control plane
DS signoff: Nora Kim validates test power calculations for two representative experiments and confirms thresholds produce <5% type-I risk across the test matrix
Eng signoff: engineering confirms integration points (events, webhooks, metrics tags) and that runbook actions are implementable within Dedicated and Hosted runtimes
Security/SRE signoff: audit entries and KMS usage for sensitive evaluation outputs are documented and approved
regression_thresholds: Quality (text-generation): cohort-level mean acceptability drop >= 2.0 percentage points triggers warning; >= 4.0 percentage points triggers throttle; >= 6.0 points triggers immediate rollback
Safety: any validated toxic or PII-signal rate increase (absolute) > 0.1% with confirmed classifier precision >= 85% -> immediate fail-open and pager
Latency: p95 increase > 30% AND absolute increase > 200ms -> throttle traffic; p95 increase > 60% -> rollback
Cost: per-token cost increase > 15% for a sustained 12h window -> alert and schedule mitigation
Embedding regressions: average cosine similarity drop > 0.03 for heavy cohorts (n>=1000) -> investigate; >0.06 -> throttle
ab_criteria: Primary metric must show significance with two-sided test at alpha=0.01 (predefined per-metric) and minimum detectable effect aligned with threshold definitions
Sequential canary gating: 3-stage rollout (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with evaluation windows at each stage. Progression requires no sentinel in the previous stage for the full observation window
Minimum sample sizes: global 10k impressions for primary metrics; cohort min n=500 for cohort-level decisioning; when sample size is below min, flag as 'insufficient data' and do not progress
Stopping rule: if any safety sentinel is triggered at any stage, immediate stop and rollback to prior model version with incident created automatically
orchestration_playbook: Stage 0: Pre-rollout smoke (internal canary) for 1h. If any critical sentinel triggers -> abort rollout and create incident
Stage 1: External canary 1% traffic for 6h with live monitoring. Critical sentinel -> immediate rollback. Medium sentinel -> throttle to 0.1% and notify owners
Stage 2: Ramp to 10% for 12h. Continue monitoring. Multiple non-critical warnings across >2 cohorts -> pause ramp and require triage
Stage 3: 50% for 24h. If metrics stable -> final 100% after 48h observation and DS signoff
Cooldowns: after any remediation action, enforce a 24h cooldown before a new rollout of the same change
notes: 2025-02-11: Draft shared with DS; initial feedback requests more granular cohort definitions for enterprise customers (Nora)
2025-02-13: Eng architecture sync: Mei flagged that p99 latency is expensive to compute for all canaries; agreed to compute p95 and sampling p99 for heavy cohorts
2025-02-15: Security review request opened (SEC-4821). Omar requested encrypted storage for raw evaluation outputs in Private deployments
2025-02-18: Met with Solutions and CS; they requested a lightweight summarization webhook to embed into customer-facing incident templates
2025-02-19: Added acceptance threshold refinement per DS: require bootstrap CI for small cohorts and Bayesian posterior checks for sparse-sample cohorts
decisions: Use tiered canary (1%/10%/50%) rather than single-step 10% to reduce blast radius
Safety sentinels are high-priority and always cause immediate mitigation; quality sentinels are graded (warning -> throttle -> rollback)
Stat testing: default to two-sided bootstrap for skewed metrics; use standard t-test for well-behaved aggregated ratios after transformation
Multiple comparisons handled by gating (sequential) rather than global FDR correction to preserve signal for small cohorts
